title: Structured referral templates and lean redesign of gastroenterology referral triage at a regional central intake
subtitle: Lean redesign with value stream mapping and A3 problem solving before the template goes live
statement: A regional central intake receives about 9,400 gastroenterology referrals a year from 160 family practices; 22 percent are returned for missing information and the median time to a triage decision is nine working days. A structured electronic referral template is ready to switch on. The intake wants to redesign triage with lean methods first, so that the template is one countermeasure within a redesigned process rather than a change that simply moves work into family practices.
whoAffected: Adults referred for gastroenterology assessment, including those with suspected cancer; family doctors and practice staff; triage nurses, gastroenterologists and booking clerks.
whatHurts: Returned referrals delay assessment, some are never re-sent, and triage nurses spend much of their time chasing information; family practices see returned referrals as lost work.
currentPractice: Free-text letters and faxes, triaged by two nurses and a gastroenterologist; missing information leads to a returned referral without a tracked queue.
whyNow: The template can be released on the next monthly schedule, and a lean coach is assigned from January to March 2027.
constraints: No research funding; a lean coach for three months from January 2027; changes to the referral template go through the digital health office's monthly release schedule; triage nurse time cannot increase.
patientCenteredGoal: Every referred patient gets a triage decision quickly, and no referral is lost between the practice and the intake.
summary: Problem framed as a lean redesign of referral triage with the template as one possible countermeasure.
